## bioRxiv
An MCP server for accessing bioRxiv and medRxiv preprint servers.

This server provides:
- Tools: Search preprints, get preprint details, list subject categories
- Prompts: Analyze preprint methodology and findings

bioRxiv is a preprint server for biological sciences operated by Cold Spring
Harbor Laboratory. It hosts research manuscripts that have NOT undergone peer
review. This server wraps the official bioRxiv API to provide structured access
to preprint metadata, abstracts, and full-text PDFs.

TOOL SELECTION GUIDE:
• search_preprints: Find preprints by date range and/or subject category (no keyword, author, or full-text search) - primary discovery tool
• get_preprint: Get full details for a specific preprint by DOI
• get_categories: List available subject categories for filtering
• search_published_preprints: Find preprints that have been formally published in journals
• funder_search: Find preprints by funding source (NIH, etc.)
• get_statistics: Usage and submission statistics

MULTI-TOOL WORKFLOWS:
For comprehensive literature analysis:
1. Use search_preprints to find relevant preprints by date range and category
2. Use get_preprint for detailed information on promising results
3. Use search_published_preprints to check if preprints have been peer-reviewed and published
4. Use funder_search to identify research funding patterns in a field

For tracking research trends:
1. Use get_categories to identify relevant subject areas
2. Use search_preprints with date filters for recent activity
3. Use get_statistics to understand submission volumes

## Claude_Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>

<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>

<?claude block s1?>

<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

## Consensus
Consensus is a research paper search engine: relevance-ranked semantic search over 400M+ peer-reviewed papers (Semantic Scholar, OpenAlex, PubMed). Use the `search` tool to look up papers for a scientific query; it takes plain-language queries and returns ranked paper records. When presenting search results, you MUST cite papers inline using their numbered references from the tool result (e.g. [1], [2], [3]). When discussing findings, always attribute them to specific papers: 'Caffeine improves endurance performance [1] and reduces perceived exertion [3].' At the end of your response, list all cited papers as numbered references with their titles hyperlinked to the URLs from the tool result: [1] [Paper Title](url) (Authors, Year, Journal, Citations). Use the exact paper URLs from the tool result — do not modify, shorten, or regenerate them. Do not omit paper links or summarize results without citing specific papers. IMPORTANT: Some search results end with a sign-up, upgrade, or usage message. When a result has one, you MUST include it at the END of your response word-for-word: do not omit, shorten, or rephrase it. When a result has none, do not add one: never write your own upgrade prompt, search count, or Consensus link. Batch at most 3 search calls at a time to avoid rate limits. For a broad request (a review, screening, finding everything on a topic), make one search with a large page_size rather than many narrower searches. If you receive a rate limit error, wait 30 seconds before retrying. Do NOT apply search filters (year_min, year_max, study_types, domain, human, sample_size_min, sjr_max, controlled, sjr_min, citation_min, open_access, country) unless the user explicitly requests them or clearly expresses intent to narrow results. If the user asks a research question without mentioning filtering criteria, call search with only the query parameter.

## github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

## Google_Drive
This is an MCP server provided by Drive API. The server provides tools for developers to build LLM applications on top of Drive.

import json,glob,collections as C
R=[]
for f in sorted(glob.glob('adjudication-*.jsonl')):
    a=f.split('-')[1]
    for i,l in enumerate(open(f)):
        d=json.loads(l); d['_a']=a; R.append(d)
print(len(R))
for k in ('verdict','status','resolution'):
    print(k,C.Counter(r[k] for r in R))
print('unify',C.Counter(r['unify'].split(':')[0].strip() if r['unify'].startswith('U-new') else r['unify'] for r in R))
print(C.Counter((r['verdict'],r['resolution']) for r in R))
print('by area res',{a:dict(C.Counter(r['resolution'] for r in R if r['_a']==a)) for a in 'ABCDEFG'})
print([r['unify'] for r in R if 'new' in r['unify']])
# duplicates
print('dups',[k for k,v in C.Counter((r['file'],r['line']) for r in R).items() if v>1])
PY

import json,glob,re,os
R=[]
for f in sorted(glob.glob('scratchpad/session_2026-11-13-edmonton-checklist-pass/sweep/adj/adjudication-*.jsonl')):
    a=f.split('adjudication-')[1][0]
    for l in open(f): d=json.loads(l); d['_a']=a; R.append(d)
pat=re.compile(r'best[ _-]?practice|ideal|most accommodating|most forgiving|acceptab',re.I)
sel=[r for r in R if (r['verdict']=='CONFLICT' and r['resolution'] in('AMEND','TOOL')) or r['resolution']=='OWNER-Q' or r['verdict']=='HELD']
print(len(sel))
bad=[]
for r in sel:
    p=r['file']
    if not os.path.exists(p): bad.append(('MISSING',r['_a'],p,r['line'])); continue
    L=open(p,errors='replace').read().split('\n')
    n=r['line']
    if n>len(L): bad.append(('PASTEOF',r['_a'],p,n)); continue
    win=' '.join(L[max(0,n-2):n+1])
    if not pat.search(L[n-1]): bad.append(('NOTERM-ON-LINE','win' if pat.search(win) else 'nowin',r['_a'],p,n,L[n-1][:100]))
for b in bad: print(b)
print('bad',len(bad))

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""scripts/audit/supersession_backpointer_audit.py — currency lives at the superseded text.

WHY THIS EXISTS (RC3, DR-2026-09-26-recurring-defect-shapes-remediation.md section 4).
Binding text lives in more than five stores (DRs, the append-only ledger, the YAML
register, the `decisions` table, CLAUDE.md, the research contract and its SessionStart
copy, code comments, `sessions/*.md`), and a ruling superseding one of them was sometimes
left with no local mark: a reader who reaches the superseded sentence by grep meets it
with nothing saying it no longer holds. The fix is not a currency INDEX — that would be
the next store rule 5 forbids — it is a pointer at the text itself, anchored on quotes
that occur exactly once at both ends, checked with plain file I/O so `.ignore` cannot
hide the target (owner rulings live overwhelmingly in `sessions/`, which `.ignore` hides
from ripgrep and the Grep tool).

THE GRAMMAR, read from the ledger and from any DR using the same trailer:

    SUPERSEDES: <target path> :: "<verbatim quote from the target>"
      BY: references/project-standards.md :: "<verbatim quote from the superseding ruling>"

NORMALISATION (so a quote survives comment wrapping, YAML folding and Markdown
blockquotes): for each line, strip leading whitespace and one leading run of `#`, `>`,
`//` or `--`, join the lines with spaces, and collapse whitespace. Both quotes must
occur EXACTLY ONCE in their own file under this normalisation.

FAILS when: the target quote occurs 0 times (edited in place, which the append-not-edit
practice forbids) or more than once (ambiguous); the BY quote does not occur exactly
once in the ledger; or no line in the target quote's own paragraph, or in the paragraph
or blockquote immediately after it, both names SUPERSEDED or AMENDED and carries the BY
quote verbatim. `BY` is always required — `DATE:` lines in the ledger are not unique
(the most repeated closes thirteen entries), so a marker cannot be anchored on one.

EXAMINED counts `SUPERSEDES:` lines. Today there may be none in a fresh clone before the
first seed lands — that is NOTHING-IN-SCOPE, not a failure (CLAUDE.md section 5a): a
check with no subject must say so, not pass by finding nothing to check.
"""
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
sys.path.insert(0, str(REPO_ROOT / "scripts"))
import dbcore                                                        # noqa: E402

LEDGER = REPO_ROOT / "references" / "project-standards.md"
DR_DIR = REPO_ROOT / "decisions"

# The grammar and normalisation are ONE home, scripts/dbcore.py (rule 5): this script and
# scripts/db.py's dispose-adversarial-finding (OWNER-RULED) both anchor on the same
# quotes and must count them the same way, or a ref that passes one refuses the other.
_SUPERSEDES_RE = dbcore.LEDGER_SUPERSEDES_RE
_MARKER_WORD = re.compile(r'\b(SUPERSEDED|AMENDED)\b')


def _paragraphs(text: str):
    """[(start_line, end_line, normalised_joined_text)], blank-normalised-line delimited.

    A blockquote's blank line is often `>` alone, which normalises to "" here too, so a
    blockquote paragraph is delimited the same way as a plain-prose one.
    """
    lines = text.split("\n")
    # script, via dbcore.count_ledger_quote, not as a raw substring: a marker paragraph
    # that wraps the quote across two comment lines (a leading `#`/`>` on the wrapped
    # line) would otherwise never match, and a correctly-authored marker would FAIL.
    return bool(_MARKER_WORD.search(raw)) and dbcore.count_ledger_quote(raw, by_quote) > 0


def _parse_supersedes(text: str):
    """[(target_path, target_quote, by_path, by_quote), ...] from one file's raw text."""
    return [(m.group(1), m.group(2), m.group(3), m.group(4))
            for m in _SUPERSEDES_RE.finditer(text)]


def main() -> int:
    sources = []
    if LEDGER.exists():
        sources.append(LEDGER)
    if DR_DIR.exists():
        sources.extend(sorted(DR_DIR.glob("*.md")))

    entries, text_cache = [], {}
    for src in sources:
        text = src.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        text_cache[src] = text
        for target_path, target_quote, by_path, by_quote in _parse_supersedes(text):
            entries.append((src, target_path, target_quote, by_path, by_quote))

    examined = len(entries)
    print(f"SUPERSEDES lines found (ledger + decisions/*.md): {examined}")
    if examined == 0:
        print("VERDICT: PASS — NOTHING-IN-SCOPE (no SUPERSEDES line exists yet; "
              "correct until the first seed lands, per DR-2026-09-26 section 8).")
        print("EXAMINED: 0")
        return 0

    if not LEDGER.exists():
        print(f"[ERROR] no ledger at {LEDGER.relative_to(REPO_ROOT)}, but SUPERSEDES "
              f"lines were found. Cannot verify BY quotes.")
        print(f"EXAMINED: {examined}")
        return 2
    ledger_prose = dbcore.strip_supersedes_citations(text_cache[LEDGER])

    findings = []
    target_cache = {}  # target_rel -> (text, paragraphs, lines); several entries can share one target
    for src, target_rel, target_quote, by_path, by_quote in entries:
        where = f"{src.relative_to(REPO_ROOT)} (SUPERSEDES {target_rel!r})"
        if target_rel not in target_cache:
            target_file = REPO_ROOT / target_rel
            if not target_file.exists():
                target_cache[target_rel] = None
            else:
                text = target_file.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
                target_cache[target_rel] = (text, *_paragraphs(text))
        cached = target_cache[target_rel]
        if cached is None:
            findings.append(f"{where}: target file does not exist.")
            continue
        target_text, paras, lines = cached
        n_target = dbcore.count_ledger_quote(target_text, target_quote)
        if n_target != 1:
            findings.append(
                f"{where}: target quote occurs {n_target} time(s) in {target_rel} "
                f"(must be exactly 1) — {'edited in place' if n_target == 0 else 'ambiguous'}.")
            continue

        if by_path != "references/project-standards.md":
            findings.append(f"{where}: BY names {by_path!r}, not the ledger — only the "
                            f"ledger is a superseding-ruling home this audit verifies.")
            continue
        n_by = dbcore.count_ledger_quote(ledger_prose, by_quote)
        if n_by != 1:
            findings.append(
                f"{where}: BY quote occurs {n_by} time(s) in the ledger's substantive "
                f"prose, excluding SUPERSEDES citation lines (must be exactly 1).")
            continue

        quote_norm = dbcore.normalise_quote_text(target_quote)
        pidx = _find_paragraph(paras, quote_norm)
        if pidx is None:
            findings.append(f"{where}: could not locate the target quote's own paragraph "
                            f"in {target_rel} (internal inconsistency — the quote counted "
                            f"once but no paragraph contains it normalised).")
            continue
        candidates = [paras[pidx]] + ([paras[pidx + 1]] if pidx + 1 < len(paras) else [])
        marked = any(_paragraph_has_marker(lines, s, e, by_quote) for s, e, _ in candidates)

    would want it — named, not silently patched with a curated exception list.'
  note: 'Advisory until OQ-3 is answered and one clean batch has passed it clean

# governance/stage-map.yaml — which pipeline stage each table belongs to.
#
# NAMED AND SIZED BEFORE IT WAS BUILT. `architecture/meta-scripts-spec.md` §8
# ("The single v2 blocker: there is no stage map") specifies this file: "one
# entry per table and view naming its stage id from pipeline-contract.yaml, with
# a `pointer:` list for cross-stage views. It is one file, ~89 lines." It names
# three consumers blocked on it — L1.8 (rule 5 checked mechanically, which today
# cannot be computed at all because stage attribution does not exist), L2.6 and
# L3.5. The judgments below were first made inside tools/pipeline_walk.py, which
# put them where none of those three could read them; this is that move.
#
# JUDGED, NOT DERIVED — and the distinction is load-bearing. There is no
# derivable table→stage edge in this repository. Two routes were measured and
# both are noise: FK topology (depth 0 holds 26 tables spanning five stages) and
# "which stage's checks read this table" (17 of 89 objects attributed, 12
# unambiguous, evidence_sources landing in four stages at once — §8's own
# measurement). Rule 8 says derive it or NAME WHO JUDGED IT. This names them.
#
# THE FALSIFIER IS THE POINT, and it is what dbcore.WRITABLE_TABLES lacked when
# it went blind eight times. The consumer reads the live table list from
# sqlite_master, not from this file: a table here that the schema lacks, a table
# the schema has that is missing here, and a stage id the contract does not
# define are each reported and each fail `workplan/pipeline-state-graph/build_graph.py
# --check`. The original falsifier, tools/pipeline_walk.py, was deleted with the render
# apparatus (plan step 1.1); no registered check reads this file until step 4.4 registers
# its successor. A new table is mapped here in the PR that adds it, by review until then.
#
# `infrastructure` is not a stage. It marks tables recording the repository's own
# operation — migration ledgers, run records — rather than pipeline content.
#
# STILL OWED: the 20 views. §8 specifies a `pointer:` list naming the stages each
# cross-stage view spans, because CLAUDE.md §3 calls a cross-stage view "the most
# protected object in the schema" and tells you to ask what it spans before
# deleting it. Five such views currently have no reader at all. Views are absent
# from this file and its consumer filters `type='table'`, so nothing yet checks

# .ignore — cold storage. Hides frozen records from ripgrep-based SEARCH only.
#
# READ THIS BEFORE CONCLUDING A FILE DOES NOT EXIST.
#
# WHAT THIS DOES AND DOES NOT DO
# ------------------------------
# Honours it (file becomes unsearchable):   ripgrep, and Claude Code's Grep tool.
# Ignores it (file stays fully visible):    git, `grep -r`, `git grep`, `ls`,
#                                           Claude Code's Glob tool, and ALL of
#                                           this repo's own Python tooling, which
#                                           walks with glob/pathlib and never
#                                           reads this file.
#
# So: nothing is deleted, untracked, moved, or hidden from code. Every path below
# is still committed, still versioned, still on disk, still opened by whatever
# opened it before. `scripts/validate_cross_refs.py` still globs
# references/search-log/; `scripts/item_audit_pipeline.py` still reads
# versions/current/. This file separates "visible to code" from "visible to agent
# search", which is why it can cover directories that could never be physically
# moved.
#
# WHY
# ---
# The repo's operative problem is not disk. It is that a session greps for a fact,
# gets several answers, and cannot tell which is current — the former CLAUDE.md §9
# guardrail 1 recorded that a stale anchor in an old document caused a real error.
# (That section was removed by the 2026-08-19 rewrite; the reasoning now lives in
# §2(b) and in §7's trap note about this very file. Pointer corrected 2026-08-22 —
# COMMENT ONLY, no entry below was added, removed or altered.) Every
# directory below holds FROZEN RECORDS: text that was true on its date and is
# preserved unedited on purpose. A hit from one answers a current question wrongly.
#
# The scope is not invented here. Every entry is already on the global
# `exempt_paths` list in governance/retired-vocabulary.yaml, i.e. already
# adjudicated, entry by entry with reasons, as an immutable record whose retired
# vocabulary is licensed rather than a defect. This file mechanises a judgement the
# repo had already made in prose.
#
# NOT hidden, deliberately: decisions/ (the governance changelog §9 tells sessions
# to read), dated workplan/ files (they ARE the current plan), attestations/, and
# scripts/migrations/ — a migration answers "which change dropped this column?"
# with a TRUE hit, so hiding it would remove a right answer, not a wrong one.
#
# SYNTAX NOTE, verified 2026-08-06 rather than assumed: a bare `dir/` entry cannot
# be re-included by a later `!dir/keepthis` line — gitignore semantics do not
# re-include a file whose parent directory is excluded. The `dir/**` form CAN be
# negated. Both negations below therefore use `**`, and both were tested with a
# planted token before this file was committed.
#
# Changing the ENTRIES in this file is OWNER-GATED: it shapes what every future
# session is able to see, and that is a judgement about the work-product, not about
# code. See decisions/DR-2026-08-06-cold-storage-search-scope.md, which is the
# ratified authority for this file's scope.
#
# Corrected 2026-08-22: this read "same as a retirement (CLAUDE.md §9 guardrail 4)"
# and pointed at CLAUDE.md §10. BOTH SECTIONS WERE REMOVED by the 2026-08-19
# rewrite, and guardrail 4 was not merely renumbered — §1 INVERTED it. Retiring
# code, checks and scripts is no longer owner-gated at all; it needs evidence, not
# permission. The owner gate on THIS file survives on its own footing (search scope
# is a work-product judgement), not by analogy to a guardrail that no longer exists.

# --- retired-but-preserved -------------------------------------------------
_archived/
workplan/_superseded/

# --- dated reports, frozen at their date -----------------------------------
audits/
references/audits/

# --- append-only research and session records ------------------------------
# Both pointers stay visible. LATEST-RESEARCH is read by the BLOCKING
# citation_mining_session check and LATEST by everything session-scoped that is
# not that gate (W4, 2026-08-06); a session debugging either must be able to find
# the file it resolves. The session RECORDS behind them stay hidden — those are
# append-only history, and a grep that surfaces forty of them to answer one
# question is the cost this file exists to remove.
sessions/**

# --- agent transcripts -----------------------------------------------------
# Owner ruling 2026-09-03, on the measurement rather than on principle: with 19 MB of
# JSONL searchable, `REF-00977` returned 174 hits of which 136 were transcripts, and
# `next_ref_id` 305 of which 194. Transcripts are CONVERSATION ABOUT the code, including

# finds THAT a transcript exists and which agent, role and time it belongs to, and the
# file itself is one `git grep` or one open away. Nothing here is deleted, untracked or

def band(tier: int, evidence_type: str) -> EvidenceMarker:
    """A source's evidence band, per tier-system section 5.

    FULL: T1, T2, Co-1, Co-2 and T3 clinical. PARTIAL: T4, T5 (a policy or standards basis,
    not primary evidence). WEAK: T3 other than clinical (grey literature) and T6 (the code
    floor). The T3 split is the one place the type matters.
    """
    if tier in (1, 2):
        return EvidenceMarker.FULL
    if tier == 3:
        return EvidenceMarker.FULL if evidence_type == "clinical" else EvidenceMarker.WEAK
    if tier in (4, 5):
        return EvidenceMarker.PARTIAL
    if tier == 6:
        return EvidenceMarker.WEAK
    raise TierDerivationError(f"no band for tier {tier!r}")

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Check that every atom's `quote` occurs verbatim in its `source` file.

usage: verify_atoms.py atoms.jsonl [--repo /home/user/guidebook]
Whitespace is collapsed and a leading blockquote marker ('> ') on each source line is ignored.
Prints one line per failure and a summary. Exit 1 if any failure. It checks the QUOTE only --
whether the atom's `claim` is a fair reading of the quote is a judgment this script cannot make.
"""
import json, re, sys
from pathlib import Path

repo = Path("/home/user/guidebook")
args = [a for a in sys.argv[1:] if not a.startswith("--")]
if "--repo" in sys.argv:
    repo = Path(sys.argv[sys.argv.index("--repo") + 1]); args = [a for a in args if a != str(repo)]

# Unified resolution plan: best / ideal / most accommodating / most common / floor

**What I checked.** All counts below come from commands over the seven `adj/adjudication-*.jsonl` files, re-run by `python3 -I` with `collections.Counter`.
- 500 records; no duplicate (file, line) pairs.
- Verdict: CONFLICT 288, NOT-CONFLICT 156, HELD 56.
- Resolution: SUPERSEDE 200, LEAVE 199, AMEND 80, OWNER-Q 10, TOOL 6, DELETE 5.
- Unify: U6 144, U1 96, U5 96, U2 82, U3 24, U4 18, U9 17, U7 14, U8 9. No adjudicator used a new key.
- The 200 SUPERSEDEs are spread over 85 files.

**Spot-checks.**
- Mechanical check of 141 records: every CONFLICT with AMEND or TOOL, every OWNER-Q, every HELD, and every DELETE. All 141 file:line pairs exist. 140 lines contain the term. The other, `assess_cell.py:1469`, has the hyphenated "most-accommodatingly".
- I also read 50 passages by hand in their own files, across all seven areas, including 9 lines no sweep flagged.
- I found no wrong citations. I did find substantive errors in some replacement wording, reconciled in section R below.

**Later owner answers applied** (the ledger at `references/project-standards.md` 7173 to the end, plus the coordinator's relays):
- The harm test.
- "T4 only half circle".
- "determination means to determine the ideal…": the word "determination" stands.
- "stage tools should match the actual name of the stage".
- "whatever doesn't matter", answering three naming questions: no aliases after a rename; the verb is "states the ideal and grades its evidence"; the stage stays "specification".

## 1. CANONICAL DEFINITIONS (one home each; everything else points to it)

**Which file holds what.** The definitions live in three governance files. The evidence for the choice:
- `governance/evidence-architecture.md:2` calls itself "CANONICAL … the single entry point to the evidence architecture", and it already holds the direction-aware selection (§5) and invariant I3.
- CLAUDE.md §9 sends doctrine to `mission-and-epistemics.md` and markers to `tier-system.md`.

The ledger stays the record of the owner's words; the governance file holds the operative text and quotes the ledger heading.

| Key | Canonical statement (owner's words) | Home |
|---|---|---|
| U1 best | "best practice IS the same as ideal IS the same as most accommodating": "the one that best responds to an ICF/access need/identity within whatever context", "identified in our research … enough if the research source itself simply asserts the value". Tier sets marker and weight, never eligibility. The one exception: "does the research prove that the more accommodating value leads to worse results? if so, research wins. if no, code wins." | New `evidence-architecture.md` §0 "The figures of a cell" |
| U2 most common | "convergence is not evidence of best practice but most common practice"; "convergence just means values coming together", across any tiers. | §0 holds the sentence; the definition of convergence stays in `evidence-methodology.md` §3.2 (T-068 rewrites it) |
| U3 floor | "the minimum is a factual data point"; "minimum is code stratum unless there is no code data"; "the minimum in some contexts may be the highest allowable number". | §0 |
| U4 figures and direction | "we just have minimum, mode, median, maximum"; "value direction of parameter matters". The best is the maximum in accommodation order. | §0 |
| U5 show, don't rule | "we gather and show"; "showing data, not determining … acceptable isn't relevant as that's a value judgment". A determination "means to determine the ideal within the context of all evidence factors and consequently what to choose and how to grade quality of evidence for it": it states the ideal and grades its evidence, and is never a verdict on a design. "Must" and "should" said of a design remain verdicts. | `mission-and-epistemics.md` commitment 2 and the posture section |
| U6 code-only | "if the only values are from code then code determines the ideal/best", the most accommodating code value; "the empty circle makes it clear that it's not academically or clinically derived". | §0 (now a special case of U1 plus the harm test) |
| U7 markers | ● T1, T2, Co-1, Co-2; ◐ T3, T4 ("T4 only half circle"); ○ T5, T6. ⚠ (U+26A0, no FE0F) takes the circle's place for a grey, unverified or thin basis. Thin is "when the evidence doesn't directly concern someone but is conjecture", including the project's own inferences and any value that "mixes". A vetted clinician's judgment, or a clinician's or academic's derivation, is not thin. | `tier-system.md` §5; code home `schemas/tier_derivation.py` `band()`; CLAUDE.md §6 points to it |
| U8 transparency | "presents all values … provides citations … does not claim with own authority". | `mission-and-epistemics.md` (same place as U5) |
| U9 names | A stage's tools "should match the actual name of the stage". The stage stays **specification** (default; owner: "whatever"). Its output is a specification; the act is "states the ideal and grades its evidence". `v_best_practice` keeps its name (see 6.Q6). | Ledger rule plus `governance/stage-map.yaml` |

## 2. AMEND LIST (R = ready now; W = waiting on applying the circle table, Q1)

Every replacement is a pointer of the form "see evidence-architecture §0", or a short phrase in the owner's words. Where an adjudicator wrote out the full definition (A, E and G did), use a pointer instead, so the definition has one home (rule 5).

**R. How I reconciled the adjudicators.**
1. Seven AMEND/TOOL replacements put a code-only best at "○" or "the empty circle". After "T4 only half circle" that is wrong for a T4 basis. All seven become "its code marker by tier".
2. A, E and G disagreed on the "mixed cell" (a code value more accommodating than every research value). The harm test settles it: code wins unless research shows worse results.
3. A and F read OR-6c as still governing the selection. The harm-test entry says it resolves OR-4 and OR-6c for selection. OR-6 and OR-6b keep their status words.
4. F's RENDER-CONTRACT:41 and A's audience-priority:80 rested partly on "authority" verbs. Under the determination ruling, choosing which value to showcase is the determination's own act. Only design verdicts remain conflicts.
5. G says EVI-184 settles the floor dispute. That is consistent with C's finding that the engine strings misname the most accommodating code value a "floor claim". Both are kept.
6. D and E both ask for the frozen corpora to be superseded file by file. I collapse that to one ledger entry per corpus (section 3).

## 3. SUPERSESSION ENTRIES

**How the audit reads a SUPERSEDES line** (`scripts/audit/supersession_backpointer_audit.py`; grammar in `dbcore.LEDGER_SUPERSEDES_RE`):
- The line is `SUPERSEDES: <one path> :: "<quote>"`, followed by `BY: references/project-standards.md :: "<quote>"`.
- The target quote must occur **exactly once** in the target file.
- The BY quote must occur exactly once in the ledger's prose (not counting citation lines). Several SUPERSEDES lines may cite the same BY quote.
- The target's paragraph, or the one after it, must carry a marker naming SUPERSEDED or AMENDED together with the BY quote.

So there are **no globs**, and every machine pair needs a marker line written into its target. The audit is advisory and reads only the ledger and `decisions/*.md`.

**One ledger entry**, "Unification 2026-11-14 — best, most common, minimum; showing and grading". Its BY sentence must be unique in the ledger, for example "the figures of a cell are read under evidence-architecture §0 from 2026-11-14". It carries:

(a) **Machine pairs, each with a marker appended after the target paragraph.** These cover the decisions/ records a live reader still reaches:
- DR-2026-05-24-best-practice-supersession-protocol.md :12, :14, :85
- DR-2026-05-26-gap-driven-mining-protocol.md:126 (flagged by no sweep)
- DR-2026-07-12-evidence-architecture-unification.md:24
- DR-2026-07-12-evidence-cell-state-schema-reconciliation.md:22, :29
- DR-2026-07-13-value-genealogy-and-derivation-handshake.md:21
- DR-2026-07-20-intra-category-cross-test.md:93
- DR-2026-07-21-evidence-architecture-option-a-execution.md:130, :132; and :15, :24, :75 when the table is applied
- DR-2026-07-20-…-weighted-strength-reconciliation.md:43 (W)
- DR-2026-07-21-product-posture-thinking-tool-not-authority.md:66 ("the practice the evidence best supports")
- RATIFICATION-PACKAGE-2026-07-12.md:8, :45

Posture DR:45 is **not** superseded: the determination ruling answers it. Touching `decisions/` requires `attestations/<slug>.json` (rule 2).

(b) **Prose-only supersession**, because there are no globs and no marker can be placed. The entry names each path or glob:
- `references/bpc/**` (D: 102 records; the files already carry FROZEN or RETRACTED banners)
- `references/audits/bpc-audit-pass0-2026-05-10.md`, `…pass2-2026-05-10.md`
- `references/connections/**`
- `references/fdr/reach-range-and-accessible-controls.md`, `references/systematic-reviews/dd1-ndv-qualitative-dd7-umbrella.md`, `references/methodology/economics-research-methodology-v1.9-archived.md`
- workplan: `2026-08-11-remediation-and-pipeline-anatomy.md` (including I3 lines 4886, 4888, 5253, 5625, 6522, W), `2026-08-12-commit-91-adversarial-review.md`, `2026-08-18-research-frame-proposal.md`, `2026-08-20-provenance-walk-execution-plan.md`, `2026-10-30-ramp-spec-pages/{owner-rules/code-baselines-accepted.md, owner-rules/spec-page-requirements.md, reports/spec-page-design-requirements-2026-10-29.md, reports/stress-test-ramp-slopes-2026-10-29__report.md}`, `2026-11-12-bidirectional-pipeline/DELEGATED-RESOLUTIONS-2-REVIEW.md`, `best-practices-assessment-system.md`, `methodology-and-pipeline-enforcement-plan-2026-07-23.md`, `next-steps-synthesis-2026-07-14.md`, `phase-e-execution-plan-v1.md`
- the three attestations F names (frozen JSON under a schema)
- `governance/mission-PROVISIONAL.md` (superseded, but has no banner), `governance/pre-stage-a-decisions.md`
- `governance/doctrine-deltas.json`: append a new state when commitment 2 is amended; do not supersede it

(c) **Ledger rules and migration rows, which can only be superseded, never edited or machine-paired.** The ledger is append-only, so no marker can sit beside its targets (the thirteenth set says the same), and migrations are immutable. The entry names:
- `project-standards.md` lines 14 ("median as default"), 17, 20, 23, 26, 142, 172, 355, 3611, 3944
